course_name_original: Elementi di calcolo delle probabilita' e statistica canale 1
course_name_en: Elements of Probability and Statistics Channel 1
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of elementary set theory and Mathematical Analysis

learning_outcomes.text: The student will be familiar with the basics of probability theory, fundamental results of the theory, and relevant models in engineering applications. They will also know the fundamental concepts of the frequentist approach to statistical induction.

The student should be able to select models to apply in simple problems from engineering practice and select appropriate statistical tools for parameter estimation and hypothesis testing on the model, using commonly used statistical software.

Although concepts are always explained in the simplest situations, any technical difficulties related to extending these concepts to more general situations are highlighted through the distribution of ad hoc material. Similarly, issues related to the foundations of statistical induction according to the frequentist approach are emphasized.
Acquire basic knowledge in probability theory.

The student will have acquired the basic notions and results related to probability theory on finite and countable spaces, the concept of discrete random vector, and the concept of continuous random variable.

The student will be able to solve simple discrete probability problems, problems inherent in discrete random vectors and random numbers represented by continuous random variables. The student will also be able to appreciate the meaning and implications of independence and conditioning (within discrete models), understand the meaning of some fundamental limit theorems, such as the law of large numbers.

The student will have the basis to analyze the analogies and relationships between the topics covered and topics of analysis and combinatorics (acquired in Analysis I courses and covered in the Foundations of Real Analysis course).
Ability to present content in the oral part of the assessment and in any theoretical questions present in the written exam.
The acquired knowledge will allow for individual study or study in a course related to more specialized aspects of probability theory.

syllabus_topics: Commonly used distributions: Binomial, Geometric, Negative Binomial, Poisson, Discrete Uniform, Uniform in (a,b), Exponential, Gamma, Gaussian, Cauchy
Fundamental limit theorems (law of large numbers, Poisson approximation and central limit theorem)
Optional topics: Introduction to Markov chains

assessment_methods.method: Written exam (problem solving and theoretical questions)

assessment_rules: To pass the exam, a score of not less than 18/30 is required. The student must demonstrate sufficient knowledge of the topics and the ability to solve at least the simplest assigned exercises. To achieve a score of 30/30 cum laude, the student must demonstrate excellent knowledge of all topics covered during the course.
bibliography: H. Hsu: Probabilità, variabili casuali e processi stocastici, Schaum's n. 93. Mc Graw Hill Italia, 1998.
Didactic material related to exercises will be distributed.
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Informatica e Automatica (L-8)
